findings.title: Queries are interpolated a second time via runSplitQuery
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates targets with applyTemplateVariables. Each shard sub-request is then passed to runSplitQuery, which now calls applyTemplateVariables on every target again. Interpolation is not idempotent. Ad-hoc filters are injected into the expression twice, and `$` or `\` characters that appear in already-expanded values get re-expanded or re-escaped. Both layers also need to interpolate in the same order, which this change does not guarantee. This is the reason the test now expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times. The call count is a symptom of the double work.

findings.title: Interpolation happens before grouping, but the request keeps raw targets
findings.body: Only the derived group requests carry interpolated targets. trackGroupedQueries still receives the original `request`, so tracking sees uninterpolated queries. This may be fine, but the existing tests that compare the tracked request now depend on the mock's applyTemplateVariables returning the same object. Separately, the new `.map` can mutate the input targets, because the test mocks mutate and return the query. If the real implementation shares references, a retry or re-run could see already-interpolated targets.

findings.title: Test asserts a brittle call count that encodes the double interpolation
findings.body: `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` locks in the redundant applyTemplateVariables calls (1 up front plus 4 inside runSplitQuery). It would fail if the double interpolation were fixed, and it does not verify correctness.
